experience.organization: Picasso Lab, University of California, San Diego
experience.role: Graduate Student Researcher, LLM Inference Systems
bullets: Built a trace-driven simulator, with attention costs fitted to measurements on H100s, that compares 40 combinations of data, tensor, context and expert parallelism; on agentic traces the fastest layout kept changing during a run, while on chat traces one layout stayed fastest.
Reproduced FlashMoE under skewed expert routing, showing that tokens exceeding a GPU’s fixed expert capacity are dropped.
Developing agentic workloads and baselines to evaluate a design that reduces synchronization barriers at the dispatch and combine steps of MoE layers.

experience.role_detail: Full-time through Apr 2024; volunteer research collaborator through Nov 2024
bullets: Architected a Python/AsyncIO training framework for 1,000+ worker nodes, with synchronous and asynchronous aggregation through a pluggable event-driven state machine.
Designed a Redis-backed parameter server with stateless workers, reducing per-round overhead to 1.7% at 1,000+ nodes versus 54.9% for an open-source baseline.
Built gRPC and MQTT worker discovery, heartbeat-based liveness detection, incremental checkpointing, and hot failover; a standby server recovered a session within 820 ms.
Validated training across NVIDIA Jetson GPUs and ARM edge devices using CNN, LSTM, and ALBERT models; tolerated about 40% worker dropout with negligible accuracy impact.
Deployed Flotilla across a containerized cluster of 1,000+ concurrent clients and contributed architecture and scalability analysis published at HiPC 2023 and JPDC 2025.
Refactored Docker images on Linux CI/CD pipelines, reducing image size by 35% and build time by 50%.
Integrated Liquibase to track MongoDB schema changes across environments.

projects.title: Distributed Container Snapshotting
bullets: Built Chandy-Lamport snapshots of live containers using CRIU/Podman checkpoints across nodes.

Implemented a transparent reliable-UDP sidecar with sequencing and retransmission; tested multi-host snapshot and restore on a counter app whose shared value stayed consistent under concurrent traffic, delay, and packet loss.

projects.title: GPU Kernel Performance and Portability
bullets: Implemented FlashAttention-2 and RMSNorm in Helion, Triton, Gluon, and CuTe; benchmarked throughput and utilization across four NVIDIA GPU generations.
Profiled kernels with Nsight Compute and compared portability, finding A100-tuned Triton/Gluon configurations lost memory throughput on T4.

Used ARMv8 cycle counters for nanosecond-scale scheduling and syscall measurements, accounting for timing overhead.
